nodes.description: Private uint256 holding the secret number (1-10) used to decide whether a player wins.
Public timestamp of the last play() call, used by kill() for the time-lock check.
Public price (0.1 ether) a player must send to play().
Address of the contract owner, set in the constructor; gates kill().
Public array of Game structs recording every bet (player address and guessed number).
Constructor: sets ownerAddr to msg.sender and initializes the secret number via shuffle().
Internal function computing secretNumber from sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1)) % 10 + 1.
Payable game entry point: validates bet, records the game, pays out the whole balance on a correct guess, reshuffles and updates lastPlayed.
Owner-only function that selfdestructs the contract if at least one day has passed since lastPlayed.
Payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers and enables the external call target used by the payout.
Caller-controlled address used as player, owner, payout recipient and destruct beneficiary.
block.timestamp, used both as a randomness source in shuffle() and as the time-lock condition in kill().
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance): sends the entire contract balance to the caller with a fixed 2300 gas stipend.
suicide(msg.sender): destroys the contract and forwards the remaining balance to the caller.
The uint256 guessed number passed to play(), constrained to <= 10 and compared to secretNumber.
Memory Game struct built inside play() from msg.sender and the guessed number before being pushed to gamesPlayed.
Pseudorandom value derived from sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1)), fully predictable/manipulable by miners and attackers.

edges.reason: play() receives the guessed number as its untrusted numeric parameter.
The parameter is validated by require(msg.value >= betPrice && number <= 10) inside play().
game.number = number copies the player guess into the local Game struct.
play() reads secretNumber and compares it with the guessed number to decide the payout.
play() writes the completed Game struct into the public gamesPlayed array.
game.player = msg.sender stores the caller identity in the local Game struct.
The caller address msg.sender is the recipient of the whole contract balance in the payout.
When the guess matches secretNumber, play() executes msg.sender.transfer(this.balance); state (lastPlayed, reshuffle) is updated only after the transfer.
The external transfer hands control to the caller, whose fallback can re-enter play() before lastPlayed/shuffle state is refreshed.
The payout external call can invoke the payable fallback of the receiving contract, providing a re-entry surface.
The constructor reads msg.sender to initialize the owner.
ownerAddr is set directly from the untrusted caller address in the constructor.
The constructor calls shuffle() to initialize secretNumber.
shuffle() writes the derived value into secretNumber.
shuffle() derives its randomness from block.timestamp (now), a miner-influenceable value.
block.timestamp is an input to sha3(now, block.blockhash(...)), making the random value miner-manipulable.
The weak pseudorandom expression is truncated to uint8, modulo 10 and assigned to secretNumber.
After each attempt play() calls shuffle() to pick a new secret number.
lastPlayed is assigned directly from block.timestamp (now) at the end of play().
play() updates the lastPlayed state variable after the payout and reshuffle.
kill() compares block.timestamp (now) against lastPlayed + 1 days, a timestamp-dependent condition.
kill() reads lastPlayed as the baseline for its one-day time-lock check.
kill() reads ownerAddr in the authorization check msg.sender == ownerAddr.
kill() authorization depends on the untrusted caller address msg.sender matching ownerAddr.
kill() executes suicide(msg.sender) once the owner and time-lock conditions hold.
The caller address determines the beneficiary of the suicide() selfdestruct.

normalization_plan.reason: The guessed number parameter is only meaningful as an argument of play(); it must be merged into the play() function node for core reasoning.
The local Game struct is a temporary container written and consumed entirely inside play(); it should be merged into the play() function node.
